$comment: Minimal READ-ONLY ABI for TinjauRiskRegistry, transcribed by hand for the reference
consumer in this directory. It is deliberately NOT generated from, imported from, or
symlinked to Tinjau's Foundry build output (contracts/out/**) or to any TypeScript in
apps/server/**. A stranger who has only the chain and this file can read the record.
Write functions (postAssessment, setPaused, rotateAssessor, setAssetSupported) are
omitted on purpose: a consumer of a risk record never needs them, and shipping them
would invite a reader to become a writer.
Each entry carries an explicit 4-byte selector so the consumer needs no keccak256
implementation at runtime. Verify any of them yourself with Foundry, e.g.
tools/risk-reader/test/anvil-e2e.sh re-derives all twelve with `cast sig` and fails if

functions.note: The record exactly as stored. RiskRecord is an all-static tuple, so it is ABI-encoded inline as 12 consecutive 32-byte words with no head offset. assessedAt == 0 means the record was never written.
The state to act on now, with expiry and the duration cap applied. May differ from the stored state; that difference is the point.
ASCII packed into bytes32, e.g. 'tinjau.risk/1.0.0'. Tells a consumer which decoder to apply.
Pause blocks NEW protections. It does not cancel a protection already running and does not erase history.
Public getter for the bounded-action envelope. Lets a consumer check the fee band and duration cap itself instead of trusting a claim about them.
keccak256(abi.encodePacked(asset, poolId)). The consumer recomputes nothing; it asks the chain.
Takes the key, not (asset, poolId). Used with envelope().cooldown to see whether a new protection could re-arm right now.
